== vendor/con-ron/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean#L168-L185
   168  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Level.lean:164-169 isEquiv — `Level.isEquiv`
   169  at two level HANDLES, with the verdict cached on the pair.  `none` is
   170  con-leche's fuel exhaustion and is never cached. -/
   171  def lvlEq? (u v : LIdx) : AM (Option Bool) := do
   172    let s ← get
   173    match s.caches.lvlEqC[(u, v)]? with
   174    | some r => pure (some r)
   175    | none => do
   176      let lu ← readLevelM u
   177      let lv ← readLevelM v
   178      match Level.isEquiv lu lv with
   179      | some r => do
   180        let s ← get
   181        let mp := s.caches.lvlEqC
   182        let s := { s with caches := { s.caches with lvlEqC := ∅ } }
   183        set { s with caches := { s.caches with lvlEqC := mp.insert (u, v) r } }
   184        pure (some r)
   185      | none => pure none

== ConAgua/L/ModelGen.lean#L12-L65
    12  /-!
    13  # Generated word models and specs (`l_model`)
    14  
    15  `l_model` reads the `lfn` text of a group of L functions and generates, for each function `f`,
    16  
    17  * its **word model** `fW : Nat → Mem → Word → … → Option (Word × Mem)` (`Option Word` for a
    18    read-only function, `ro`; no fuel argument for a single function that needs none): the L code
    19    with every local inlined, `abort` as `none`, a load as `rdW`, a store as `Mem.set64`, a call to a
    20    group member as that member's model at fuel `n`, a call to another function as the model its
    21    spec states (`specs`), and the code after an effectful call as a first-order continuation
    22    `fW.k_g` (`| none => none | some (x, m₁) => …`) over the locals it reads, named after the
    23    callee `g` (`fW.k_g_2`, … for its later calls, in source order; after a loop `fW.k_loopᵢ`), so
    24    that a change elsewhere in the code does not rename it. The code after an `if`
    25    whose branches both fall through is a join point `fW.jᵢ` over the locals and the memory (no
    26    copy of it). Equal continuations of the group are shared;
    27  * a function with **several results** (`return (a, b, …)`) gets a list model
    28    `Option (List Word × Mem)` (`return e` is `some ([e], m)`, the end of the body `some ([], m)`;
    29    `↦ fW list` forces it), or with `↦ fW tuple` a tuple model `Option (Word × … × Mem)` (the
    30    longest `return`'s arity, shorter ones padded with `0`); a function **without results**
    31    (`↦ fW void`, its returned values ignored) gets `Option Mem`, read-only `Option Unit`, and the
    32    spec states `fW n s₀.mem args = some s'.mem` (`= some ()` with the memory unchanged);
    33  * a **loop** (`while c { … }` in the `lfn`, or a spliced named block `⟪X⟫` that is one `while`)
    34    is a model of its own, `fW.loopᵢ n m x₁ …` (`exec p n` on the loop: `| 0 => none | n + 1 =>
    35    if c then … fW.loopᵢ n … else exit`; the enclosing code applies it at `n + 1`), over the locals
    36    live at its head. Its result is `(signal, outs…, memory)`: the signal (`Sig.normal`,
    37    `Sig.ret vs`) if the body has a `return`, the locals it assigns that the code after it reads,
    38    the memory unless read-only; the code after it is a continuation of that result. A loop with a
    39    `return` followed by the function's last statement (`return …`, `abort`) is **fused**: its model
    40    returns the function's result. Its spec `fW.loopᵢ.spec` (`⦃s = s₀⦄ exec p n X ⦃…⦄`, by
    41    induction, the model is the loop's meaning) is generated, and a `while` written in the `lfn`
    42    becomes the named block `fW.loopᵢ.stmt` (with `fW.lfn_eq : F = lfn … ⟪fW.loopᵢ.stmt⟫ …`).
    43    Named blocks without a loop are inlined;
    44  * one **guarded equation** `fW.armᵢ` per non-`none` leaf of the `if` tree of each model, loop and
    45    continuation (the path's conditions as hypotheses, in order; on the negative side in their
    46    natural form: `a = b` for `¬ a ≠ b`, `a ≠ b` for `¬ a = b`, `p` for `¬ ¬ p`), each with a `grind_pattern` in the
    47    `grind` attributes; `fW.abortᵢ` for each `none` leaf, `fW.k_g.none` for each continuation (no
    48    patterns);
    49  * the **spec** `⦃s = s₀⦄ invoke p (exec p n) "f" args ⦃LocEq s' s₀ ∧
    50    fW n s₀.mem args = some (r.headD 0, s'.mem); ⊤⦄` of every member (`some (r, s'.mem)` for a list
    51    model, `some (r.headD 0, r.tail.headD 0, …, s'.mem)` for a tuple model), as one conjunction
    52    over the group (`name`), a step theorem per member (`name.stepᵢ`: `vcgen` with the specs of the
    53    callees and loops that member calls, then `vc_flat` and `grind`, below) and the induction on the fuel.
    54  
    55  The definitions come in dependency order: each strongly connected component of the reference
    56  graph is one definition or one `mutual` block, well-founded on `(fuel, depth)` if it has a
    57  continuation or a loop (models `(n, D)`, continuations `(n + 1, d)`, loops `(n, d)`; `LevelLeq.lean`
    58  does this by hand), structural on the fuel if it has only models.
    59  
    60  ```
    61  l_model liftGo_spec (p : Prog) (hp : LiftProg p)
    62    fns [(hp.get "lift_go") ↦ liftW, (hp.get "lift_app") ↦ liftAppW]
    63    specs [derBv_spec p (hp.get "der_bv") n, memoFindG_spec lfSch p _ (hp.get "lf_find") n]
    64    grind [arena_grind] fold [tierW, idxW] finish [tierW, idxW] gen 20 heartbeats 1000000
    65  ```

== ConAgua/Arena/ArenaRel.lean#L285-L308

== ConAgua/Arena/ConsLibRel.lean#L11-L31
    11  /-!
    12  # The cons-table library: the relation and the user API (lane conslib)
    13  
    14  A cons table `C` (`ConsLib.lean`) represents the arena's two `Tbl`s of one constructor (the twin's
    15  `HashMap2`s: persistent and scratch) by **`ConsR C R m on P Q`**: both tiers hold the same nodes
    16  in the same order (node `i` of tier `t` related to `nodes[i]` by the instance's record relation
    17  `R`), the same key → handle map, the node counts at `CTL[ca + t]`, the scratch flag `CTL[1]` is
    18  `on`; and the slots index the nodes (the slot layout, the probing and the growth state, which no
    19  user sees). The L model of every `intern_X` is `consInternM C m ks` (`ConsLibSpec.lean`).
    20  
    21  Both are irreducible outside this file: the lemmas below are the whole interface.
    22  
    23  * **Reading the relation**: `ConsR.flag`, `ConsR.ctl`, `ConsR.cnt`, `ConsR.cap`, `ConsR.rec`,
    24    `ConsR.cons`, `ConsR.back`, `ConsR.recSize`, `ConsR.node`, `ConsR.cons_hit`.
    25  * **Keeping it**: `ConsR.frame` (a writer apart from the table), `ConsR.setFlag` (`CTL[1]`),
    26    `ConsR.reset` (the scratch reset), `consR_init` (the all-zero memory), `ConsR.congr`.
    27  * **An interning**: `consIntern_correct` (it refines the arena's hash-consing, from the
    28    instance's obligations `ConsKeyOK`), `consInternM_frame` (what it writes), `consInternM_word`,
    29    `consInternM_lt`, `consInternM_pw` (the handle word), `consInternM_out` (a hit, or the append
    30    of node `cntC`: the memory outside the slot array is `pushRec`).
    31  

== ConAgua/L/WriteSet.lean#L14-L31
    14  /-!
    15  # Write sets from the program text
    16  
    17  `Preserve.lean` proves once that a program without `st8` keeps the byte arrays and the sizes.
    18  The same induction gives a frame for every function of a *call-closed* set `fs` whose bodies
    19  store only into word arrays of `A` and into words of the control array `ctl` listed in `C`. A
    20  `ctl` index must be a literal `k`, or `k + (e &&& 1)`, which can only be `k` or `k + 1` (the
    21  tier-indexed counts of the stores, `CTL[k + (t & 1)]`). The check `closedW` is a `Bool` function
    22  of the text, so a concrete program's write set is `by decide +kernel`.
    23  
    24  The frame itself is abstract here (`WFrame`): any reflexive relation on memories closed under
    25  the allowed stores. `Arena/Frame.lean` instantiates it with `MemFrame` (the arena's layout:
    26  `CTL` is array 1). Lane `scale`'s spike, made layout-agnostic (DESIGN.md, "The relation's architecture").
    27  
    28  Global variables (`GVar`) are not restricted by `closedW` (a `WFrame` is closed under every global
    29  write). Their write sets are lists of names, `closedG p G fs` (section "Global variables" below):
    30  every run of `f ∈ fs` keeps the globals outside `G` (`GFrame`), and `Triple.gframe` adds that to a
    31  callee's spec for its caller's `vcgen`.

== ConAgua/L/Agree.lean#L600-L604
   600  /-- **Non-interference for `L.run`.** -/
   601  theorem run_agree {p : Prog} {S : TieredArray → Bool} {S8 : ArrId → Bool} {fs : List FnName}
   602      (hp : readsIn p S S8 fs = true) {f : FnName} (hf : f ∈ fs) (n : Nat) (vs : List Word)
   603      {m₁ m₂ : Mem} (hm : Agree S S8 m₁ m₂) :
   604      RunAgree S S8 (run p n f vs m₁) (run p n f vs m₂) := by

== ConAgua/L/Agree.lean#L7-L31
     7  /-!
     8  # Non-interference: runs that read only agreeing arrays agree
     9  
    10  `readsIn p S S8 fs` is a `Bool` check of the program text: every function of `fs` that `p`
    11  defines calls only into `fs`, and every array its body names (loaded, stored, measured, copied
    12  from or to, scanned) is a word array of `S` or a byte array of `S8`. The array sets are
    13  predicates (`S : TieredArray → Bool`, `S8 : ArrId → Bool`; a list `l` is `l.contains`). A
    14  tiered access `a⟨t⟩` names both tiers, `↑a` and `tier1 a`. Global variables are not restricted.
    15  (`Stmt.rdOk` takes the callee set as a predicate too: `readsIn` uses membership in `fs`, the
    16  per-function split for a large program (`Compiler/ReadSetSplit.lean`) a tree of name codes.)
    17  
    18  `Agree S S8 m₁ m₂`: the two memories have the same word arrays in `S`, the same byte arrays in
    19  `S8`, and the same globals. Everything else (other arrays, the number of arrays) may differ.
    20  
    21  **The theorem** (`invoke_agree`): for `f ∈ fs` of a set that passes `readsIn`, two runs of
    22  `invoke p (exec p n) f vs` from states that agree (memories `Agree`, equal locals) end the same
    23  way: the same error, or the same returned values from final states that agree again. `run_agree`
    24  is the same for `L.run`. The proof is the frame proof's induction (fuel, then statements): every
    25  read sees equal data, every write writes equal data to an array of `S`/`S8` (or a global).
    26  
    27  Why: lane parmode (docs/design/parmode.md, Step 4, piece (b2)). A worker runs `check_pending`
    28  in a memory in which only the frozen images and the worker's own arrays have content; every other
    29  array is empty. That memory agrees with the full sequential memory on `S` = frozen ∪ owned, so
    30  the worker's run is the sequential one, which the sequential proof covers.
    31  -/

== ConAgua/Checker/Pipeline.lean#L49-L53
    49  /-- **A relational stage spec**: from memory satisfying `Pre`, a returning call of `f` keeps the
    50  caller's locals and ends in memory satisfying `Post r`. -/
    51  def RelSpec (p : Prog) (f : FnName) (Pre : Mem → Prop) (Post : List Word → Mem → Prop) : Prop :=
    52    ∀ (n : Nat), n ≤ 2 ^ 62 → ∀ (s₀ : St), Pre s₀.mem → ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ invoke p (exec p n) f []
    53      ⦃fun r s' => LocEq s' s₀ ∧ Post r s'.mem; ⊤⦄

   347    r7 : R7 (ConAgua.Final.loadMem b pb sz) m₇ pb ds ipins sE

   351    grow : BKeep m₇ m

== ConAgua/Checker/Pipeline.lean#L74-L77
    74  /-- What every stage may assume of the inputs: a 64-bit platform, both buffers below `2^63`
    75  bytes, every word array below `2^64` words. -/
    76  def InputsOK (b pb : ByteArray) (sz : TieredArray → Nat) : Prop :=
    77    System.Platform.numBits = 64 ∧ b.size < 2 ^ 63 ∧ pb.size < 2 ^ 63 ∧ ∀ s, sz s < 2 ^ 64

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L9-L34
     9  /-!
    10  # The compiler from L to Kraken x64
    11  
    12  See DESIGN.md, "The compiler". One pass: an expression is evaluated straight into its target
    13  register by `gen`, with scratch registers; where `gen` does not apply, into `rax` with
    14  intermediate values in fixed per-frame temporary slots (`compileE`).
    15  
    16  **Machine state during L code.**
    17  * `r15` = `T`, the address of the run's descriptor table (`Tab`); pinned.
    18  * `r14` = the fuel counter; decremented at every loop back-edge and every call.
    19  * `rsp` = the current frame; constant while a body runs. Local `x` is the word at `rsp + 8x`,
    20    temporary `t` is at `rsp + 8(nlocals + t)`. The frame has `frameWords` words.
    21  * `rbp` = the trampoline's saved stack pointer; never written by L code.
    22  * `rbx`, `r12`, `r13`: free; the trampoline saves and restores them for its caller.
    23  * `rax` = expression result, `rcx`/`rdx` = scratch, `rsi` = argument pointer at a call.
    24  
    25  **Exits.** `ca_error`, `ca_abort` and `ca_exhausted` are global; they restore the caller's `rsp`
    26  from `rbp` and return to the harness with `rdx` = 2, 2 resp. 1. `ca_abort` is an error whose code
    27  (`Err.code`) is in `rbx` (`abort e`, `if c abort k`: `if c abort k` sets `rbx` before the test
    28  and keeps its one conditional jump; the test itself keeps `rbx`), `ca_error` one with code `0` (a
    29  bounds check, a bare `abort`); both return the code in `rax`. `abort e` may overwrite any
    30  register, a leaf's locals in `rbx` included (nothing after an abort reads a local), but `if c abort
    31  k` writes `rbx` also when it does not abort: it does so only where no local lives in `rbx`
    32  (`Ctx.rbxFree`, `sim_ifAbortK`); in a leaf that keeps a local there it is the general `if`. A
    33  normal return has `rdx` = 0 and the result in `rax`.
    34  -/

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L2138-L2159
  2138  def trampoline (tab : Tab) (entry : FnName) (c np : Nat) : Program :=
  2139    [.label enterL,
  2140     movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np)) .r15, movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np + 8)) .rbx,
  2141     movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np + 16)) .r12, movMR (mb .rdi (tab.save np + 24)) .r13,
  2142     i64 (.push (oR .rbp)), i64 (.push (oR .r14)), i64 (.push (oR .rdi)),
  2143     movRR .rbp .rsp, movRR .r15 .rdi, movRR .r14 .rsi,
  2144     movRM .rsp (mb .r15 Tab.stackTop),
  2145     i64 (.lea (rr .rsi) (mb .r15 tab.args))] ++
  2146    (if np ≤ argRegs.length then loadArgs tab 0 (argRegs.take np) else []) ++ burnFuel ++
  2147    [i64 (.call (.rel (.sub (.label (fnL entry)) .after_current_instruction))),
  2148     jmpL okL,
  2149     .label exhaustedL, movRI .rdx 1, jmpL finishL,
  2150     .label errorL, movRI .rbx 0,
  2151     .label abortL, movRR .rax .rbx, movRI .rdx 2,
  2152     .label finishL, movRR .rsp .rbp,
  2153     i64 (.pop (.reg (rr .r15))),
  2154     movRM .rbx (mb .r15 (tab.save np + 8)), movRM .r12 (mb .r15 (tab.save np + 16)),
  2155     movRM .r13 (mb .r15 (tab.save np + 24)), movRM .r15 (mb .r15 (tab.save np)),
  2156     i64 (.pop (.reg (rr .r14))), i64 (.pop (.reg (rr .rbp))),
  2157     i64 .ret,
  2158     .label okL] ++ loadRes { tab, fn := entry, nl := 0, brk := okL } 0 c (tab.nres - c) ++
  2159    [movRI .rdx 0, jmpL finishL]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L804
   804  def allocRegs : List Reg64 := [.rdi, .r8, .r9, .r10, .r11, .rsi, .rbx, .r12, .r13]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L2109-L2121
  2109  def compileFn (tab : Tab) (t sk : NTree) (f : FnName) (fd : FunDecl) : Program :=
  2110    let ctx := fnCtx tab t sk f fd
  2111    let F := fd.nlocals + tempsS ctx.alloc ctx.nr fd.body
  2112    if frameless fd then [.label (fnL f)] ++ fnBody ctx fd ++ [i64 .ret]
  2113    else if ctx.leaf && sk.find (nameCode f) == some F then
  2114    [.label (fnL f), i64 (.sub (.reg (rr .rsp)) (oI (8 * F)))] ++ fnBody ctx fd ++
  2115    [i64 (.add (.reg (rr .rsp)) (oI (8 * F))), i64 .ret]
  2116    else
  2117    [.label (fnL f),
  2118     movRR .rax .rsp, i64 (.sub (.reg (rr .rax)) (oM (mb .r15 Tab.stackLimit))),
  2119     i64 (.cmp (.reg (rr .rax)) (oI (8 * F + 8 + 8 * ctx.need))), jccL .c exhaustedL,
  2120     i64 (.sub (.reg (rr .rsp)) (oI (8 * F)))] ++ fnBody ctx fd ++
  2121    [i64 (.add (.reg (rr .rsp)) (oI (8 * F))), i64 .ret]

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L99-L160
    99  /-- **The layout check**: `l` lists the array at each of the `nb + nw` positions, `m` maps each of
   100  them to its position and nothing else (an entry `k ↦ v` has `v` in range and `l[v]` of code `k`),
   101  the byte positions `[0, nb)` hold tier-0 names, and a tier 1 sits at a word position right after
   102  its tier 0. -/
   103  def layOkB (nb nw : Nat) (l : List TieredArray) (m : NTree) : Bool :=
   104    l.length == nb + nw &&
   105    m.all (fun k v => decide (v < nb + nw) && (l[v]?.map TieredArray.code == some k)) &&
   106    (List.range (nb + nw)).all (fun i => m.find (arrAtD l i).code == some i) &&
   107    (List.range nb).all (fun i => !(arrAtD l i).hi) &&
   108    (List.range (nb + nw)).all (fun i => !(arrAtD l i).hi ||
   109      (decide (nb < i) && arrAtD l (i - 1) == TieredArray.t0 (arrAtD l i).arr))
   110  
   111  /-- The number of result registers. -/
   112  def maxRes : Nat := 6
   113  
   114  /-- The layout of the descriptor table at `T`:
   115  * `[T]` the initial stack pointer (top of the stack region), `[T + 8]` its lower limit;
   116  * `[T + 16 + 8p]` the base of the array at descriptor position `p < nb + nw` (`Tab.dbase`), then
   117    `[T + 16 + 8 (nb + nw) + 8p]` its length (`Tab.dlen`), in bytes for a byte position (`p < nb`),
   118    in words for a word position, then `[T + 16 + 16 (nb + nw) + 8p]` a word position's length in
   119    32-bit elements (`Tab.dlen32`, twice its length in words: the bound of a 32-bit access);
   120  * then the constant data `rom` (the byte strings of the program's `ldc` reads), padded to whole
   121    words;
   122  * then the result area: results `maxRes, maxRes + 1, …, nres - 1` of a call, one word each (empty
   123    if `nres ≤ maxRes`);
   124  * then the global variables `0, …, ng - 1`, one word each;
   125  * then the arguments of the entry function, one word each.
   126  
   127  (`nres` is not part of the table in memory: it says how many results the code passes.) -/
   128  structure Tab where
   129    /-- The byte positions `[0, nb)`. -/
   130    nb : Nat
   131    /-- The word positions `[nb, nb + nw)`. -/
   132    nw : Nat
   133    /-- The array at each position (`Tab.wAt`; a byte array `a` as `↑a`). -/
   134    arrAt : List TieredArray
   135    /-- The layout map: `s.code ↦` the position of `s` (`Tab.pos64`, `Tab.pos8`). -/
   136    lmap : NTree
   137    /-- The map and the position list agree (`layOkB`). -/
   138    layOk : layOkB nb nw arrAt lmap = true
   139    rom : List UInt8 := []
   140    /-- The number of results in use: the most results any `return` gives or any call reads. The
   141    first `maxRes` go in registers (`resReg 0`, …), the rest in the table's result area. -/
   142    nres : Nat := 1
   143    /-- The number of global variables: global `g` (with `g.id < ng`) is the word at `globOff g`. -/
   144    ng : Nat := 0
   145    /-- Minimum lengths (`L.ArrDecl.min`): `(s.code, k)` says that word array `s` has at
   146    least `k` words in every layout the code runs in (`Layout.Ok.min64`; the entry stubs establish
   147    it), so a constant index below `k` needs no bounds check (`Tab.min64`). -/
   148    mins : List (Nat × Nat) := []
   149    /-- The table-relative array (`L.ArrDecl.atTable`): `(a, c)` says that tier 0 of word array `a`
   150    starts at `T + c`, past the table and the trampoline's save area, in every layout the code runs in
   151    (`Layout.Ok.tbl64`; the entry stubs place it there), so the code addresses it from `r15` without
   152    loading its base. -/
   153    tbl : Option (ArrId × Nat) := none
   154    /-- `rom.length`, stored: the offsets past the constant data (`resOff`, `globOff`, `args`) are
   155    then arithmetic on the table's fields, and the kernel does not count the bytes of a large ROM
   156    each time it evaluates the code generator (DESIGN.md, "Kernel-checked compiler output"). -/
   157    romLen : Nat := rom.length
   158    romLen_eq : romLen = rom.length := by rfl
   159    deriving Repr, DecidableEq
   160  

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L170-L182
   170  /-- The byte arrays a program may name (a byte position), and their positions. -/
   171  def Tab.dom8 (t : Tab) (a : ArrId) : Bool :=
   172    match t.lmap.find (TieredArray.t0 a).code with
   173    | some p => decide (p < t.nb)
   174    | none => false
   175  def Tab.pos8 (t : Tab) (a : ArrId) : Nat := (t.lmap.find (TieredArray.t0 a).code).getD 0
   176  
   177  /-- The word arrays a program may name (a word position), and their positions. -/
   178  def Tab.dom64 (t : Tab) (s : TieredArray) : Bool :=
   179    match t.lmap.find s.code with
   180    | some p => decide (t.nb ≤ p)
   181    | none => false
   182  def Tab.pos64 (t : Tab) (s : TieredArray) : Nat := (t.lmap.find s.code).getD 0

== ConAgua/Compiler/Step.lean#L11-L19
    11  /-!
    12  # One instruction at a time
    13  
    14  The compiler proof is a forward simulation on Kraken's own judgment
    15  `Eventually (step1 Host.exe) Q ⟨d, pc⟩` ("every run from `d` at `pc` reaches `Q`"), for an
    16  arbitrary `Host` program that contains the compiled code. Each lemma here steps over one
    17  instruction form the compiler emits, in continuation-passing style: the hypothesis is the
    18  `Eventually` at the next state, the conclusion the `Eventually` at this one.
    19  -/

== ConAgua/Compiler/Rel.lean#L144-L167
   144  /-- L's memory `m` in the machine's data memory `d`. The machine side (`Layout`, the table) is
   145  positional; L's arrays are names, related to their regions through the compiler's layout map
   146  (`Tab.pos8`, `Tab.pos64`): the array a program may name (`dom8`, `dom64`) has the region of its
   147  position. -/
   148  structure MemRel (G : Layout) (m : Mem) (d : DataMem) : Prop where
   149    size8 : ∀ a, G.tab.dom8 a → (m.arr8 a).size = G.s (G.tab.pos8 a)
   150    size64 : ∀ s, G.tab.dom64 s → (m.arr64 s).size = G.s (G.tab.pos64 s)
   151    get8 : ∀ a, G.tab.dom8 a → ∀ (i : Nat) (h : i < (m.arr8 a).size),
   152      d.get? (A (G.b (G.tab.pos8 a) + i)) = some (m.arr8 a)[i]
   153    get64 : ∀ s, G.tab.dom64 s → ∀ (i : Nat) (h : i < (m.arr64 s).size),
   154      rdW d (A (G.b (G.tab.pos64 s) + 8 * i)) = some (m.arr64 s)[i]
   155    limit : rdW d (A (G.T + 8)) = some (UInt64.ofNat G.lo)
   156    /-- The descriptors, by position: no L array in them. -/
   157    base : ∀ p < G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw, rdW d (A (G.T + (G.tab.dbase p).toNat)) = some (UInt64.ofNat (G.b p))
   158    len : ∀ p < G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw, rdW d (A (G.T + (G.tab.dlen p).toNat)) = some (UInt64.ofNat (G.s p))
   159    /-- A word position's length in 32-bit elements. -/
   160    len32 : ∀ p, G.tab.nb ≤ p → p < G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw →
   161      rdW d (A (G.T + (G.tab.dlen32 p).toNat)) = some (UInt64.ofNat (2 * G.s p))
   162    rom : ∀ (i : Nat) (h : i < G.tab.rom.length),
   163      d.get? (A (G.T + 16 + 24 * (G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw) + i)) = some G.tab.rom[i]
   164    stack : ∀ x, G.InStack x → (d.get? (A x)).isSome
   165    res : ∀ x, G.InRes x → (d.get? (A x)).isSome
   166    /-- The global variables. -/
   167    glob : ∀ g : GVar, g.id < G.tab.ng → rdW d (A (G.globAddr g)) = some (m.glob g)

== ConAgua/Compiler/Rel.lean#L71-L85
    71  /-- The regions are inside the address space and pairwise disjoint, every word array the program
    72  may name has at least its minimum length (`Tab.min64`, the hint the code generator drops
    73  constant-index bounds checks by), and the table-relative array (`Tab.tbl64`) starts where the
    74  code addresses it, at `T + c`. -/
    75  structure Ok : Prop where
    76    tab_end : G.tabEnd < 2 ^ 64
    77    hi_le : G.hi < 2 ^ 64
    78    lo_le : G.lo ≤ G.hi
    79    end_ : ∀ p < G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw, G.b p + G.tab.wd p * G.s p < 2 ^ 64
    80    tab_stack : ∀ x, G.InTab x → ¬ G.InStack x
    81    tab_arr : ∀ x, G.InTab x → ¬ G.InArr x
    82    stack_arr : ∀ x, G.InStack x → ¬ G.InArr x
    83    disj : ∀ p < G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw, ∀ q < G.tab.nb + G.tab.nw, p ≠ q → ∀ x, G.In p x → ¬ G.In q x
    84    min64 : ∀ s, G.tab.dom64 s = true → G.tab.min64 s ≤ G.s (G.tab.pos64 s)
    85    tbl64 : ∀ s c, G.tab.dom64 s = true → G.tab.tbl64 s = some c → G.b (G.tab.pos64 s) = G.T + c

== ConAgua/Compiler/Abi.lean#L8-L41
     8  # The entry stubs (lane `abi`)
     9  
    10  The harness's whole job shrinks to: map a zero region, hand over the two input buffers, call
    11  `ca_start(in, in_len, pins, pins_len, base, base_len)` once. `ca_start` is the sequential driver
    12  (`parStub`, below): it calls entry 1 and then entry 2 on the same region. Both go through the
    13  setup stub `ca_setup` (`abiStub`, an internal label; the argument registers as `ca_start`'s),
    14  emitted before the trampoline, which sets up inside the region everything the harness used to lay
    15  out (`L.Compiler.Tab`), then tail-jumps into the trampoline `ca_enter(T, fuel)`:
    16  
    17  * System V arguments: `rdi`/`rsi` = the input bytes (the byte array at descriptor position `0`),
    18    `rdx`/`rcx` = the pin-data bytes (position `1`; ignored if the program has one byte array), `r8` =
    19    `base`, `r9` = `base_len`. Returns `rax`/`rdx` as `ca_enter` does. Which arrays sit at positions
    20    `0` and `1` is the layout map's business: the final theorem's proof checks that they are the
    21    input's and the pin data's (`ConAgua/Final/Abi.lean`).
    22  * If `base_len < abiNeed`, or if `in_len` or `pins_len` is `2^63` or more (the top bit of `rsi`
    23    or `rcx` set: `cmp r, 0; jl`), it returns at once with `rdx = 1` (resources exhausted; never
    24    accept). So a run that gets past the stub has both buffers below `2^63` bytes, which the
    25    refinements assume (`InputsOK`).
    26  * The region is a static partition into `abiSlot`-byte slots (no allocator; the pages that are
    27    never touched never become real): slot `0` is the table (`T = base`), slot `1` the L stack
    28    (`abiStack` bytes at its bottom), then one slot per descriptor position past the two buffers, in
    29    position order (`Tab.slotOf`). Each array starts at its slot's start; its length is `abiSlot`
    30    bytes, resp. `abiWords` words. The table-relative array (`Tab.tbl64`) lies instead inside slot
    31    `0`, past the table, with its minimum length (`abiOff`, `abiSz`); it has the last position, which
    32    gets no slot (`Tab.nslot`).
    33  * The constant data is written into the table by immediate stores (no `.rodata` read); the result
    34    area and the global variables are the region's zeros.
    35  * The fuel is `abiFuelM = 2^62 - 1 - abiInl` (`compile_correct` takes any `N < 2^62`): the run of the
    36    inlined program it stands for is a run of the program with `abiFuel = 2^62 - 1` (`MainRef.lean`).
    37  
    38  Nothing here is trusted: `sim_abiStub` (`ConAgua/Compiler/AbiSim.lean`) runs the stub on the
    39  machine, `abiLayout_ok` and `abi_memRel` (`ConAgua/Final/Abi.lean`) show that it establishes
    40  `Layout.Ok`/`MemRel` for the partition, and `abi_harness` gives `compile_correct`'s premises at
    41  the trampoline. -/

    22  /-- **The checker's code**: the `.text` section of `checker.s`. -/
    23  noncomputable def checkerFile : Program := include_asm "../checker.s"

    29  namespace L.Checker

== ConAgua/Checker/Asm.lean#L42-L51
    42  /-!
    43  # The checker's machine code, as a kernel-checked literal (generated by `scripts/checker_prog.py`; do not edit)
    44  
    45  `checkerAsm : Program` is the compiled checker as a literal term, and
    46  `checkerAsm_eq : compileProgX checkerX checkerTab checkerProgI "check" = checkerAsm` is checked by the
    47  kernel, one function at a time (`asm_lit`, `ConAgua/Compiler/AsmLit.lean`; the functions' checks are in
    48  `AsmPart0` … `AsmPart17`), so running the compiler as compiled Lean code is not trusted.
    49  `checkerFile_eq` (`ConAgua/Checker/AsmFileEq.lean`) compares it with the committed file
    50  `checker.s` (`scripts/asm_file.py`). DESIGN.md, "Kernel-checked compiler output".
    51  -/

== ConAgua/AsmFile/Include.lean#L17-L36
    17  # `include_asm "path"`: an assembler file as a `Program` (TRUSTED)
    18  
    19  `include_asm "path"` is a term of type `Program`: the `.text` section of the assembler file at
    20  `path` (relative to the directory of the current Lean file, as `include_str`), read by
    21  `parseAsmFile` (`ConAgua/AsmFile/Parse.lean`) when the term is elaborated, and turned into a term by
    22  `programTerm` (`ConAgua/AsmFile/Term.lean`). A file it cannot parse is an error.
    23  
    24  The term is cut into segments for the kernel's sake, without changing its value: a new segment
    25  starts at the label `ca_enter` (the trampoline) and at each function entry `ca_f_g`; the labels of
    26  segment `ca_f_g` are written as `lbl "g" n m` where that is their value. So the term is
    27  `stub ++ (trampoline ++ (f₀ ++ (… ++ (fₖ ++ []))))`, the shape `asm_lit`'s `checkerAsm` has.
    28  
    29  The trusted base is this parser (`parseAsmFile`): the term comes from it alone. Two independent
    30  cross-checks, not needed for soundness: Kraken's own parser must read the file's code the same way
    31  (`ConAgua/AsmFile/CrossCheck.lean`, run by `scripts/asm_file.py`: ~13 s, too slow to
    32  run here), and the assembler must encode what the file says (`scripts/check-asm.sh`). And here,
    33  the code is printed again with Kraken's printer (`toATT`) and compared with the file's `.text`
    34  lines: parse ∘ print is the identity on the file, so the parser reads every instruction the way
    35  the printer (which wrote the file) meant it.
    36  

== ConAgua/AsmFile/CrossCheck.lean#L12-L18
    12  /-! `lake env lean --run ConAgua/AsmFile/CrossCheck.lean FILE.s`: reads the file's code with both
    13  parsers, the trusted one (`parseAsmFile`, `ConAgua/AsmFile/Parse.lean`, which the final theorems'
    14  term comes from) and Kraken's own (`Kraken.X64.Parser.parse`, independent code), and fails
    15  (exit 1), naming the first differing directive, its line and function, if they disagree. A
    16  cross-check, not part of the trusted base; `scripts/asm_file.py` runs it. It is
    17  not in `include_asm`: Kraken's parser takes about 17 s on the checker's 5.3 MB there, twice the
    18  module's elaboration time (docs/design/asmfile.md). -/

== scripts/asm_file.py#L2-L21
     2  """Regenerate the two committed generated files the binary is built from (`make`, `Makefile`):
     3  
     4  * `checker.s`: the entry stub, the trampoline and the compiled checker, printed by
     5    `ConAgua/Checker/AsmEmit.lean` (run as a script, so the compiler runs as compiled Lean code;
     6    nothing here is trusted: the final theorems are about the file as the trusted parser reads it
     7    (`ConAguaAsm/Checker.lean`), and the kernel checks that it is the compiler's output,
     8    `checkerFile_eq` in `ConAgua/Checker/AsmFileEq.lean`). Regenerate after every change to the
     9    checker's L code (`ConAgua/Checker/Prog.lean`), the compiler or the stub.
    10  * `pins.bin`: the pin data `main.c` embeds, written by `romgen pins.bin 4`
    11    (`ConAgua/Rom/Gen.lean`): the checker's startup data and all of con-leche's `natOpPinSets` (4
    12    variants, the set con-ron embeds). Not trusted either: the theorems hold for every pin buffer.
    13    Regenerate after a change to the startup data or a twin bump.
    14  
    15  Both modes also run the parser cross-check `ConAgua/AsmFile/CrossCheck.lean` on `checker.s`:
    16  Kraken's own parser must read the code as the trusted parser does (~13 s; not in `include_asm`,
    17  where it would double the module's elaboration time).
    18  
    19  Usage: scripts/asm_file.py [--check] [--no-build]
    20    --check     fail (exit 1) if a file would change; do not write it
    21    --no-build  do not build ConAgua.Checker.AsmEmit's imports and romgen first"""

    18  def main (args : List String) : IO UInt32 := do

== ConAgua/Compiler/Bce.lean#L234-L258
   234  /-- The facts after `s`, `none` if it does not end normally. -/
   235  def postF : Option Facts → Stmt → Option Facts
   236    | none, _ => none
   237    | some fa, s =>
   238    match s with
   239    | .skip => some fa
   240    | .set x e => some (fa.set x e)
   241    | .st8 a i e => some ((fa.addLoads (Expr.loads i ++ Expr.loads e)).addLt (.b a) i)
   242    | .st64 a i e => some ((fa.addLoads (Expr.loads i ++ Expr.loads e)).addLt (.w a) i)
   243    | .st64t a t i e =>
   244      let fa := fa.addLoads (Expr.loads t ++ Expr.loads i ++ Expr.loads e)
   245      some (match keyT a t with | some k => fa.addLt k i | none => fa)
   246    | .st32t a t i e =>
   247      let fa := fa.addLoads (Expr.loads t ++ Expr.loads i ++ Expr.loads e)
   248      some (match key32 a t with | some k => fa.addLt k i | none => fa)
   249    | .gset _ e => some (fa.addLoads (Expr.loads e))
   250    | .seq s t => postF (postF (some fa) s) t
   251    | .ite c s t => joinF (postF (some (fa.condAll c true)) s) (postF (some (fa.condAll c false)) t)
   252    | .while c s =>
   253      let f' := fa.killAll (Stmt.writes s)
   254      if Stmt.hasBrk s then some f' else some (f'.condAll c false)
   255    | .brk | .ret _ | .abort _ => none
   256    | .call xs _ args => some ((fa.addLoads (args.flatMap Expr.loads)).killAll xs)
   257    | .scan8 x .. => some (fa.kill x)
   258    | .copy64 .. | .copy8w .. => some fa

== ConAgua/Compiler/Compile.lean#L838-L844
   838  /-- An access with key `k` and index `i` to an array of minimum length `mn` needs its bounds check:
   839  the facts do not prove `i` in range (`safeIdx`). -/
   840  def Ctx.ck (ctx : Ctx) (k : Option AKey) (i : Expr) (mn : Nat) : Bool := !safeIdx ctx.fa k i mn
   841  
   842  /-- The bounds check of index register `r` against the length at `ln`, if `ck`. -/
   843  def chkR (ck : Bool) (r : Reg64) (ln : AddrExpr) : Program :=
   844    if ck then [i64 (.cmp (.reg (rr r)) (oM ln)), jccL .nc errorL] else []

== ConAgua/Compiler/BcePost.lean#L436-L441
   436  /-- **Every run of `exec p n` keeps the facts.** -/
   437  theorem fsound_exec (p : Prog) : ∀ n, FSound fun s σ => (exec p n s).run σ
   438    | 0 => fun s σ fa r σ' h _ => by
   439      simp [exec, throw, throwThe, MonadExceptOf.throw, StateT.lift, StateT.run, bind,
   440        Except.bind] at h
   441    | n + 1 => fsound_step p (exec p n) (fsound_exec p n)

== ConAgua/Compiler/BceSound.lean#L582-L586
   582  /-- **The facts at an expression**: they hold in a state `σ0` with `σ`'s memory that agrees with
   583  `σ` on the locals `e` reads. (`σ` may be a ghost state of the expression code's proof, whose
   584  locals in clobbered registers changed, `Inv.ghost`; `σ0` is the statement's state.) -/
   585  def FactsFor (ctx : Ctx) (σ : St) (e : Expr) : Prop :=
   586    ∃ σ0 : St, FHolds ctx.fa σ0 ∧ σ0.mem = σ.mem ∧ ∀ y, Expr.readsV y e = true → σ0.loc y = σ.loc y

== ConAgua/Compiler/BceSound.lean#L629-L641
   629  /-- **The check of an access dropped by the code generator** (`Ctx.ck` false) is not needed: the
   630  index `i` (a part of `e`) is below the array's length `L`, which is at least the minimum `mn` and
   631  the key's length in the states that agree with `σ` on `e`. -/
   632  theorem ck_sound {ctx : Ctx} {σ : St} {e i : Expr} (hfa : FactsFor ctx σ e)
   633      (hsub : ∀ y, Expr.readsV y i = true → Expr.readsV y e = true)
   634      {k : Option AKey} {mn L : Nat} (hck : ctx.ck k i mn = false) (hmn : mn ≤ L)
   635      (hk : ∀ σ0 : St, σ0.mem = σ.mem → (∀ y, Expr.readsV y e = true → σ0.loc y = σ.loc y) →
   636        ∀ key, k = some key → key.len σ0 ≤ L)
   637      {j : Word} (hj : evalP σ i = .ok j) : j.toNat < L := by
   638    obtain ⟨σ0, h1, h2, h3⟩ := hfa
   639    have hs : safeIdx ctx.fa k i mn = true := by simpa [Ctx.ck] using hck
   640    exact safeIdx_sound hs h1 hmn (hk σ0 h2 h3)
   641      (by rw [evalP_congr h2 (fun y hy => h3 y (hsub y hy))]; exact hj)

== vendor/con-ron/ConRon/Arena/Pooled.lean#L20-L46
    20  /-! ## The pool, as the twin sees it
    21  
    22  The binary's check phase is not one walk but a POOL: the jobs (one per record,
    23  `recordJob` at the record's view of the stream's index) are shared among
    24  workers, and each worker runs the jobs it claimed, in increasing order, on ONE
    25  state it built with `worker_state` and threads through them.  `PooledAccepts` is
    26  that shape on the twin side: the index built, and a family of job lists — one per
    27  worker — covering every position, each accepted by `checkJobList` from the
    28  driver's state's worker.  It says nothing about which worker ran which job.  It does say that a worker's
    29  jobs increase: Theorem 1 inducts in fold order, and a job's start state is reached
    30  through the jobs its worker ran before it, whose specifications need the fold up
    31  to their own, smaller, positions. -/
    32  
    33  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:211-239 checkPool — **the pooled
    34  check, accepted** (the cited `Jobs ds justify` at `justify = none`, no solution):
    35  the index of `ds` built from `s`, ending in `s'`; and `parts`,
    36  one job list per worker, each drawn from the positions of `ds`, together covering
    37  them, each strictly increasing (the pool claims off one monotone counter), each accepted by `checkJobList` from `s'.worker`.  The twin of the Rust's
    38  `PoolAccepts` (`Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`). -/
    39  def PooledAccepts (mode : CheckMode) (pins : List INatOpPinSet)
    40      (ds : Array IDeclaration) (s : AState) (I : IStreamIndex) (s' : AState) : Prop :=
    41    ∃ (parts : List (List Nat)),
    42      buildIndex ds s = .ok (.ok I, s') ∧
    43      (∀ t < ds.size, ∃ w ∈ parts, t ∈ w) ∧
    44      (∀ w ∈ parts, ∀ t ∈ w, t < ds.size) ∧
    45      (∀ w ∈ parts, w.Pairwise (· < ·)) ∧
    46      (∀ w ∈ parts, ∃ s'', checkJobList mode pins none I ds w s'.worker = .ok (.ok (), s''))

   106  
   107  `check` reads the global `MODE`, which the entry stubs write (`Compiler/Abi.lean`): `0` (the
   108  region's zero; no entry leaves it) aborts; `1` (`ca_start_a`, entry 1) is
   109  `check_a(1)`: the stages, the stream index and `par_compact` (the frozen buffer in `OUT`,
   110  `Arena/Freeze.lean`), returning `2^63 + k` for `k` records (jobs); `3` (the sequential driver's
   111  entry 1) is `check_a(0)`, the same with the buffer's header only; `2` (`ca_check_b`,
   112  `ca_check_seq`, entry 2) is `check_b`: the jobs `PLO‥PHI-1`; `4`‥`6` `--compare`'s runs. -/

== ConAgua/Checker/Entry.lean#L149-L171
   149  /-- `check_b()`: on the worker region's first call the seed (`CTL`) from the buffer; on every call
   150  the phase's words of the seed (`CTL[128]`, `CTL[162‥173]`, `CTL[224]`: the stream index's counter,

   152  first phase's region with its own header's seed) re-read from the buffer (none in place: `CTLF`

== main.c#L169-L190
   169  /* `--jobs=N` (N > 1), the threaded mode (and the threaded compared run, `run_compare`).
   170  
   171     Entry 1 (`ca_start_a`; for a compared run `ca_start_ac`, which takes the solution's bytes as
   172     two more arguments) runs the stages and the stream index in the region. On success (rdx = 0,
   173     rax = 2^63 + k for k jobs) it has written the frozen buffer into `OUT`, whose word 1 is the
   174     buffer's length in words. The buffer stays where it is: the rest of the region is unmapped
   175     around it and the buffer is made read-only, so a write to it faults and kills the process,
   176     which is never an accept (route A). N threads then each map their own zero region and claim
   177     job indices from one atomic counter, calling `ca_check_b(buf, len, j, region, region_len)` for
   178     each claimed j, one call after the other on the region as the previous call left it. The
   179     region is ca_worker_size bytes (a compared run's buffer has two job phases; which job is in
   180     which phase is entry 2's business, not the harness's: a thread's calls of both phases run on
   181     its one region).
   182  
   183     Concurrency: the threads share only the read-only buffer, the claim counter (fetch_add hands
   184     out each of 0, 1, 2, ... once, in order, so each thread's claims increase: `ThreadsRun`'s
   185     `incr`) and a stop flag that only shortens a failing run. Each thread has its own region and
   186     its own result slot; main combines the slots after joining every thread. Accept iff no slot
   187     holds a failure: every call that thread made accepted, and the threads drain the counter past
   188     k unless one fails. Otherwise the verdict is that of the failing job with the smallest index:
   189     the indices are claimed in order and a thread finishes the job it holds, so every lower job
   190     has been run, and accepted, when the threads are joined (`ThreadFail`'s `below`). */

    35  | D18 | `Arena/RecGen.lean` `class_fields_of_go`, `class_rec_tys_ok`, `class_rules_ok`, `class_recs_rules_ok_go`, `check_block_classes_keys`, `class_majors`, `class_seeds`; `Arena/RecClass.lean` `class_gen_minor_ty_ihs_go`; `Arena/RecCheck.lean` `target_major_nfs`, `erase_each`, `block_rec_split_own_aux`, `block_rec_want_aux_names`, `tgt_stored_rules_remap`; `Arena/IndSum.lean` `check_sum_ctors`; `Arena/IndParts.lean` `block_split*`, `block_groups*`, `block_rec_want`/`_got`, `block_member_counts_go`, `block_shape_names_of`/`_ctors_of`/`_members_of`/`_rhss_of`/`_recs_of`; `Arena/IndInstall.lean` `check_block_teles`, `check_block_inds_cv_tas(_go)`, `check_block_idx_sorts`, `check_block_ctors_go`, `check_block_positivity_nfs(_member)` | `classFieldsOf`, `classRecTysOk`, `classRulesOk`, `classRecsRulesOk`, `checkBlockClasses`' `ks.mapM`, `classMajors`, `classSeeds`, `targetMajorNfs`, `targetK53`'s `mapM`s, `targetRecPins`' `filter`s and `mapM`, `tgtStoredRules`' `map`, `checkSumCtors`, the block splitters, `checkBlockTeles`, `checkBlockInds`, `checkBlockIdxSorts`, `checkBlockCtors` build their result lists by `::` (constant time per element); `checkBlockPositivity` maps `outs` | self-recursion as the twin's, each element (or record) `sl_cons`ed onto the rest's `IW` slice: a copy per element, so that every written word lies above the old pool top and the decodings stay stable | performance (quadratic in the list's length: a block's members, constructors, fields, recursors, rules; small lists) | rec2, indproofs2, indproofs3 | intent unclear: an in-place slice writer (preallocate, and a frame lemma for writes above a slice), if blocks get large |
    36  | D24 | `Arena/StrLit.lean` `str_ls1`, `str_cons_spine` (via `rom_lit`); formerly also listed as D21 and D26 | `internLsNode [u]`, `internE (.lit (.natVal c))` take the key as a value | the one-element list / one-limb literal is pushed at the pool top first and stays there even when the node already exists (one word per call) | performance (memory: two pool words per string-literal unfolding, a few per `List` test) | defeq2 | intern from a scratch word, or pop the top on a hit |
    37  | D28b | `Arena/StubNames.lean` `name_rec`, `name_rec_i`, `intern_ls_iw` | `internNNode (.str n "rec")`, `.str n s!"rec_{i}"`, `internLsNode us` take the key as a value | the string (3, or 4 + digits words) / the level list is written at the pool top (`pool_room`) and stays there even when the node exists | performance (memory: a few pool words per block member / recursor / level list built) | stubs | as D24: pop the top on a hit |
    38  | D37 | `Arena/Scratch.lean` `scratch_reset`, `Arena/MemoLib.lean` `memoClearG` | `ron/hashmap2.rs` `clear_fit`: at each per-declaration / per-call reset the table is re-made at twice a decaying high-water mark of its entries | the scratch cons tables keep their largest size (the epoch bump empties them); the memos cleared by `memoClearG` return to their default region (`MN0` slots), regions grown within a stamp stay resident. `inst_list`'s memo (`ilSch`) clears with `memoClearFitG`, the twin's policy with the default region as its floor (the twin's floor is 32 slots) | performance (a round past 3/4 of the default region grows it in place; outside `ilSch` a handful of such rounds per run on the perf fixtures and `Init`, docs/design/d37.md; memory stays resident) | unassigned | the scratch tables: a decaying high-water mark per table, shrinking the slot count at reset; the other memos: `memoClearFitG` (with the fast-path test in the caller) where a measurement shows growth |

    62  | D43 | `Arena/ConsLib.lean` the slot word (`kfHead`, `kfLoad`, `cpSlot`, `kgrowB`), `Arena/Scratch.lean` `scratch_reset` (`SCBLIM`) | con-ron task #148, `arena/cons_map.rs` `ConsMap`: a slot is `CSlot { g: u16, f: u16, h }`, `g` the table's epoch (live iff equal, at least 1), `f = frag_of(hash)` the top 16 bits of `hash · golden`; each table's `clear` bumps its own epoch and at `EPOCH_MAX = 65 535` vacates its slots (`O(capacity)`) and restarts at 1 | one 64-bit word per slot: the fragment in bits 63–48, the value `B t + i + 1` below it (a value at or below the tier's base `B t` is free), so the stamp is `B / 2^32` in bits 46–32, **15 bits**: bit 47 is the mark of the in-place growth (D38); one base `CTL[62]` for all 19 scratch tables, which `scratch_reset` raises by `2^32` and at `B ≥ 2^47 - 2^33` vacates all 19 scratch tables and restarts at `0`, i.e. every 32 766 resets (two per declaration) where con-ron wraps each table every 65 535 clears (also two per declaration); the fragment is bits 31–16 of `hash · golden`, the bits our home (`mulhi`, D36) uses least, where con-ron takes the top 16 (the bits its masked home uses least) | performance only: the wrap's `O(capacity)` zeroing comes twice as often per table; lookups and verdicts are the same (a fragment only filters which slots read their record) | ronsync2 | stays while the growth is in place (D38): the mark needs a bit above every live value, and without the growth's mark the stamp could take all 16 bits |

    72  | D55 | `Checker/CompareEntry.lean` (mode 6 or 7 before any job) | a capacity abort in the challenge's preparation happens after the solution's jobs: con-ron prints the solution's reject if one fails | the challenge's preparation runs before the solution's jobs (D53), so a class-0 abort (capacity, `error`) there is reported even if a solution job would reject | completeness (`error` where con-ron reports the solution's reject; class 0 claims nothing) | compare2 | by design (consequence of D53) |

== docs/deviations.md#L76-L107
    76  ## Fixed
    77  
    78  - **D51** (fixed by lane compare2): `--compare` takes `--jobs=N` (before or after `--compare`), as con-ron: entry 1 `ca_start_ac` freezes one store image with two headers and the threads run both phases' jobs in one pool over it (`ca_check_b`, D54, D56), covered by `checkerFile_compare_threads_accept` and `checkerFile_compare_threads_verdict` under `ThreadsRun bC (some bS) pb` (`Final/CmpThreads.lean`).
    79  - **D52** (fixed by lane compare2): the solution's jobs no longer read a copy of the frozen arrays on a separate worker region: the threads read one store image through two headers (header S, header C), the sequential run checks both phases in place (D53, D57).
    80  - **D19** (fixed by lane ronsync2, the twin bump to con-ron `01ecb31c`): an inductive's capabilities no longer carry `sortZ` (con-leche task #480: the never-zero facts are computed at use), so the ROM reader interns no `PropWhen` name.
    81  - **D40** (fixed by lane d40): the `replace_fvars` memo (`rfSch`, banked per call) kept its entries for the whole run (`rf_clear` was never called); now the outermost `replace_fvars` (caller's generation `0`) clears it on return, where the twin drops its per-call map (docs/design/d40.md).
    82  - **D4** (fixed by lane consync, helper consync-pins): con-ron ed864140 retired `orElseAttempt` (its task #129): an error inside a pin-variant attempt is the run's error in the twin too, and L's loop is the twin's boolean decision loop (`check_div_mod_pin_loop`); the attempt flag `ATT` and the `fail R` class masking are gone.
    83  - **D21, D22, D29** (fixed by lane consync, the twin bump to con-ron `ed864140`): the projection tables left the constants (con-leche task #362): no reserved table name is interned any more (`proj_table_name` is gone; tables are keyed on the structure name in the environment's table component, `find_table`), and no constant is a projection table (the ROM reader has no kind `6` to refuse).
    84  - **D39** (fixed by lane epochwrap): `scratch_reset` aborted after `2^30` resets (the slot base `B = CTL[62]` at `2^62`); now at `B ≥ 2^62` it vacates the 19 scratch slot tables (the growth's zero loop `kzeroLs`) and restarts `B` at `0`, as con-ron's `HashMap2::clear` at `EPOCH_MAX` (docs/design/epochwrap.md).
    85  - **D35** (fixed by lane tierswitch): every store keeps one word array per tier (tier `t` of array `a` is the word array `tierA a t`, `ld64t`/`st64t`): records `ra⟨t⟩[i * w + f]`, slot tables `sa⟨t⟩` (one KSTP formula per tier array), derived and level-parameter columns `col⟨t⟩[i]`, as con-ron's per-tier `Tbl`s (docs/design/tierswitch.md).
    86  - **D1** (fixed by decls3 landing 4 and lane integrate): `and_pin_ok`'s inductive arm landed (kind `6`) and `rom_and_pin` got L code, so the real `And` block is accepted.
    87  - **F1** (fixed by lane twinaudit): id tables dense + sparse (`IdTable`); ids past the end no longer abort (`e2e/rounds_huge_gaps`).
    88  - **F2** (fixed by lane front2): strings with escapes (`Unescape.lean`, `str_put_esc`).
    89  - **F3** (fixed by lane strlit): `strVal` lines.
    90  - **F4** (fixed by `nat_dec`, `ApplyExpr.lean`): `natVal` past 18 digits.
    91  - **F5** (fixed by lane front2): expression and declaration lines.
    92  - **F6** (fixed by lanes indproofs/indproofs2, landing 6): inductive lines in the front.
    93  - **F7** (fixed by lane romload): pin data as an input.
    94  - **F8** (fixed by lane decls): the readback's `EMemo` mirrored with back references.
    95  - **F9** (fixed by lane decls3): uncached `lvl_eq` in lane induct's code, now `lvl_eq_c`.
    96  - **F10** (fixed by lane whnf): the eager mode-memo take/put banks, via the eager key bit.
    97  - **F11** (fixed by lane libs): dropping the scratch tier cost O(capacity); epoch slots.
    98  - **F12** (fixed in place by lanes indproofs, decls2, indproofs2): `sl_get` out of range, `check_block_agree` on an empty rest, `pin_in` on an empty table, `class_read` wrapping.
    99  - **F13** (fixed by lane whnf2): uncached `lvls_eq` in `iota_rec_at`, now `lvls_eq_c`.
   100  - **F14** (fixed by lane indproofs2): uncached `lvls_eq` in `target_class_match` (was D7), now `lvls_eq_c`.
   101  - **F15** (fixed by helper whnf4-d23): D23, `lp_go`/`inst_lp_core` could not cut off at a parameter-free node (L's derived words kept only the two ranges), so the walk descended into parameter-free subterms and `inst_lp_core` read `ls_node(us)` for a parameter-free `e`. Now the level-parameter bit is mirrored per node (`LpCol.lean`: bit 30 of the five `XDER` words; columns 55‥61 for `succ`/`max`/`imax`/level lists/`sort`/`const`/`fvar`, written when the node is pushed; `ArenaR`'s `*Hp`/`*Lp` fields, `DerR`'s `bvP`/`zlP`), read by `der_b`'s third result (`derLW_ok`), and `lp_go`/`inst_lp_core` test it first, as `instLPGo`/`instLPFast`.
   102  - **F16** (fixed by lane defeq2): D25, `lvl_live` checked `imax` arguments with `lv_node` (a level read before a knot call was not known to read back after it). Now `PoolGrew.lvl` (the level tables only grow) rides in `CoreAfter` and `lvl_den_later` reads the level back; L mirrors the twin again.
   103  - **F17** (lane slotgrow): the cons tables (`SLOT` … `NNSLOT`) were fixed at their whole array and `X_push` aborted at 3/4 load; now they grow like con-ron's `HashMap2` (double and rehash, here at 1/2 load from 8 slots per tier, `SlotGrow.lean`), so a large slot array no longer costs memory or page faults up front.
   104  - **D18/D24** (`hoist_ok`, fixed by lane front3): the ground hoist `hoistNatOpGround` in L (`Checker/Hoist.lean`); `prepare_prelude` reorders instead of aborting (`e2e/natop_order`, `natop_before_ble`).
   105  - **F18** (lane memlay): the cons tables and the memos grew at load 1/2 (no row had recorded it); now at 3/4, con-ron's `HashMap2` load factor (`LOAD_NUM/LOAD_DEN`).
   106  - **D5** (fixed by lane harness): the harness loaded a 1-variant pin buffer; the binary now embeds `pins.bin` = `romgen pins.bin 3`, all three of con-leche's `natOpPinSets` variants, as con-ron embeds them (18 more e2e accepts, none lost); four since con-leche #578 (`romgen pins.bin 4`, lane ronsync5).
   107  - **D41** (retired by lane scanfast-p3): `fast_line`, a recogniser of lean4export's canonical byte form tried before the generic scanner, coupled the checker to the exporter's exact output; the single pass `line_rec` (`Front/LineRec.lean`) reads each line once, in any member order and spacing, as con-ron's `scan_line_loop` does.

== scripts/e2e.py#L2-L25
     2  """End-to-end differential testing of the L checker (lane `e2e`, DESIGN.md "End-to-end runs").
     3  
     4  Steps (all in _tmp/e2e/<checkout name>/):
     5  
     6  1. **Assemble.** Every `ConAgua` module (except executables and the spike) is imported, in as few
     7     import closures as the modules allow (some clash on declaration names; each clash is reported),
     8     and `ConAgua/E2E/Dump.lean` dumps every binding of an L function name to a FunDecl it finds
     9     (`Prog` lists and `p.lookup "f" = some d` hypotheses). The bindings are merged; the program is
    10     everything reachable from `check` and `check_np` (`ConAgua/E2E/Check.lean`). A called function
    11     with no L code (no binding, or only `abort` stubs) gets an e2e stub with its own code.
    12  2. **Compile.** `check`: the shipped code, printed by `checker.s`'s generator
    13     (`ConAgua/Checker/AsmEmit.lean`; the report says whether the committed file is up to date);
    14     `check_np`: `e2e-l asm` (checks `Prog.wf`). Each linked with `cc main.c` (the entry stub
    15     lays out a fixed partition of one region, lane `abi`: no capacity retries).
    16  3. **Run** every fixture (con-leche's e2e fixtures and the arena tests) through the compiled
    17     `check` and `check_np`, the reference `con-ron-lean-twin` (the twin at the program's pin list; with and
    18     without the prelude), and `L.run` (`e2e-l run`) on small fixtures; classify.
    19  4. **Report** `docs/e2e.md` (and `--csv` appends a line to `docs/e2e.csv`).
    20  
    21  Never a merge gate. Every run has a timeout; a monitor kills any run above PER_RUN_GB and the
    22  largest run while all together are above TOTAL_GB.
    23  
    24  Usage: scripts/e2e.py [--no-build] [--jobs N] [--only REGEX] [--rerun-failing [RESULTS]]
    25                       [--trace {disagree,all,none}] [--trace-sample N] [--write] [--csv]

== scripts/diff-e2e.py#L2-L46
     2  """The end-to-end differential of the shipped binary: `./checker FILE.ndjson` on every fixture of
     3  con-leche's test suite that has a pinned expectation, against that expectation. No Lean needed.
     4  
     5      scripts/diff-e2e.py [--bin PATH] [--jobs N] [--parallel P] [--timeout S] [--tests DIR] [--only REGEX]
     6                          [--refs] [--no-cache]
     7  
     8  The fixtures and the expected exit codes are con-leche's `tests/` at the revision `vendor/UPSTREAM`
     9  pins: `tests/e2e-expected.txt` ("<exit> <fixture>" under `tests/e2e/`, gzipped or not) and
    10  `tests/arena-expected.txt` ("<exit> <path>" inside `tests/arena/lean-arena-tests.tar.gz`).
    11  con-leche's exit codes are 0 accept, 1 reject, 2 decline, 3 error, 124 a deliberate non-terminating
    12  input. `--tests` names that directory (default `$CON_LECHE_TESTS`, else the tests at exactly the pinned
    13  revision, extracted from the reference clone `_tmp/ref/con-leche` with `git archive` into
    14  `_tmp/ref/con-leche-tests/<rev>/` by `scripts/conleche_tests.py`, fetching if needed; the clone's
    15  working tree is never used). An override is not checked against the pin.
    16  
    17  The checker exits 0 only on accept, 1 on a reject, 2 on a decline, 3 otherwise (`main.c`'s usage
    18  text). Its reject/decline labels follow con-ron's twin, not con-leche, so a fixture is compared on
    19  accept versus not-accept, and a reject/decline that differs from con-leche's is only counted
    20  (`kind differs`):
    21    agree         con-leche accepts and the checker accepts, or con-leche does not accept and the
    22                  checker exits 1, 2 or 3 (a run still going after T_LOOP seconds counts here when
    23                  con-leche's expectation is the non-terminating 124)
    24    UNSOUND       the checker accepts where con-leche does not
    25    INCOMPLETE    con-leche accepts and the checker exits 1, 2 or 3
    26    CRASH         a signal, or an exit code the checker never uses
    27    TIMEOUT       the run did not finish in `--timeout` seconds (and 124 was not expected)
    28  The run is green when every fixture agrees; the exit code is 0 then, 1 otherwise (2: usage, missing
    29  fixtures).
    30  
    31  `--refs` also runs con-ron (`--jobs=1`) and `con-ron-lean-twin` on every fixture and reports REFDIFF where either
    32  one's accept/not-accept differs from the checker's, or where the checker rejects or declines and con-ron
    33  does not say the same (the full differential of PLAN.md's "Verdict checks");
    34  it replaces `bench.py --reps 0`, which no longer checks verdicts. The references' verdicts depend only
    35  on the fixture and the reference binary, so they are cached in `_tmp/bench/verdict-cache/`, keyed by the
    36  fixture's content hash and the hash of the reference binary (and, for con-ron, its pins file): after the
    37  first run, `--refs` costs about as much as the plain run, until a twin sync changes a binary. Timeouts are
    38  never cached. A fixture expecting 124 gets T_LOOP seconds on every system.
    39  (`--no-cache` ignores the cache.) The references: `.lake/build/bin/con-ron-lean-twin`, built (`scripts/lake build
    40  con-ron-lean-twin`) when it is missing or older than `vendor/UPSTREAM` or `pins.bin`, so a twin bump never meets a
    41  stale one; con-ron at `$CON_RON` or `_tmp/ref/con-ron-integrate/target/release/con-ron`, refused when its
    42  checkout is not at `vendor/UPSTREAM`'s con-ron revision or the binary is older than that commit.
    43  
    44  `--jobs N` is passed to the checker (`--jobs=N`, the threaded mode; 1, the default, passes nothing
    45  and runs the sequential path). `--parallel P` is how many fixtures run at once (default 4).
    46  """

== scripts/gates.sh#L11-L24
    11  # Steps, in order (stops at the first failure):
    12  #   links       scripts/overview-links.sh            OVERVIEW.md/README.md line anchors
    13  #   vendor      scripts/bump-con-ron.sh --check      vendor/ = upstream + patches
    14  #   modules     scripts/modules_check.py             every module is built by a target
    15  #   provenance  scripts/provenance.py check          every FunDecl's twin citation is exact
    16  #   reasons     scripts/reasons.py --check           (when the script exists)
    17  #   build       scripts/lake build ConAgua           (timeout 90 min)
    18  #   warnings    scripts/lean_warnings.py --base BASE   no Lean warning in the changed .lean files (vendor/
    19  #               excluded), also for modules restored from the shared cache (their logs are in the log store)
    20  #   check-asm   scripts/check-asm.sh                 as/objdump encode checker.s as Kraken reads it
    21  #   shake       scripts/shake.py                     every import `lake shake` finds unused is allowlisted
    22  #   core-fns, loop-fns, leaf-fns, phaseb-fns, preloop-ws   the generated call closures are current
    23  #   checker-prog  scripts/checker_prog.py --no-build --check   the generated program files are current
    24  #   e2e         make checker; scripts/diff-e2e.py --parallel 16   verdicts on every fixture

== .github/workflows/ci.yml#L4-L80
     4  # WHAT THE JOBS COVER
     5  #
     6  #   checker  The shipped binary, with no Lean anywhere (a few minutes):
     7  #              make, make check   `main.c` + `checker.s` + `pins.bin` build
     8  #                                 with a C23 compiler (`#embed`), and the
     9  #                                 smoke test passes (the prelude is
    10  #                                 accepted, a malformed line is not).
    11  #              scripts/diff-e2e.py  the end-to-end differential: the built
    12  #                                 `checker` on every fixture of
    13  #                                 con-leche's test suite that has a pinned
    14  #                                 expectation (628: `tests/e2e/` and the
    15  #                                 arena snapshot), against that
    16  #                                 expectation, compared on accept versus
    17  #                                 not-accept (the checker exits 0 only on
    18  #                                 accept, and does not tell a reject from a
    19  #                                 decline).  Green is every fixture
    20  #                                 agreeing: no accept where con-leche does
    21  #                                 not accept, no non-accept where it
    22  #                                 accepts, no crash, no timeout.  Two
    23  #                                 lanes: the sequential path (the default
    24  #                                 run) and `--jobs=4` (the threaded mode),
    25  #                                 which must give the same verdicts.
    26  #            The fixtures are con-leche's own `tests/`, checked out at the
    27  #            revision `vendor/UPSTREAM` pins (sparse: `tests/` only).
    28  #
    29  #   proof    The proofs and every gate that guards the committed files:
    30  #              overview-links.sh  every line-anchored link of OVERVIEW.md
    31  #                                 and README.md still cites the recorded
    32  #                                 lines (no build);
    33  #              modules_check.py   every `ConAgua/**` module is built by
    34  #                                 some target (no build);
    35  #              bump-con-ron.sh --check  `vendor/` is exactly the upstream
    36  #                                 files at `vendor/UPSTREAM` plus
    37  #                                 `vendor/patches/` (clones con-ron and
    38  #                                 con-leche into `_tmp/ref/`);
    39  #              provenance.py check  every L function's twin citation is
    40  #                                 exact at the vendored revisions;
    41  #              scripts/lake build  the default targets: L, the compiler,
    42  #                                 the checker, every proof, the vendored
    43  #                                 con-leche and con-ron.  This includes
    44  #                                 the axiom guards (`#guard_msgs` on the
    45  #                                 final theorems' `#print axioms`), the
    46  #                                 kernel's check that `checker.s` is the
    47  #                                 compiler's output (`checkerFile_eq`) and
    48  #                                 the staleness checks of the generated
    49  #                                 call closures;
    50  #              check-no-warnings.sh  the build's log holds no warning
    51  #                                 outside Kraken (a Lake dependency);
    52  #              shake.py           every import Lean's import minimizer
    53  #                                 (`lake shake`) finds unused is on
    54  #                                 `scripts/shake-allowlist.txt`;
    55  #              the `--check` modes of the generators: asm_file.py
    56  #                                 (`checker.s` and `pins.bin` are what the
    57  #                                 generators print now, plus Kraken's own
    58  #                                 parser reading `checker.s` as the
    59  #                                 trusted parser does), core_fns.py,
    60  #                                 loop_fns.py, leaf_fns.py, preloop_ws.py;
    61  #              check-asm.sh       `as` + `objdump` encode every
    62  #                                 instruction of `checker.s` the way
    63  #                                 Kraken's semantics reads its text (a
    64  #                                 trusted-base check, about 10 s).
    65  #
    66  # WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES **NOT** COVER
    67  #
    68  #   * the differential against the two reference checkers
    69  #     (`scripts/e2e.py`: con-ron's arena checker compiled by Lean, and
    70  #     con-ron's Rust binary), and its interpreter and per-function
    71  #     sweeps: they need a Rust build of con-ron and Lean executables
    72  #     on top of the proof build, and take far longer than the verdict
    73  #     sweep above, which already compares every fixture with the
    74  #     pinned expectation.
    75  #   * `scripts/bench.py` and the `Init` benchmark: an export of `Init`
    76  #     is not in the repository, and a shared runner measures noise.
    77  #     Timings are measured with `perf stat` on a quiet machine.
    78  #   * the progress census (`scripts/census.py`) and the build
    79  #     statistics: reports, not gates.
    80  #
